member.name: ComputeMarkBeforeJingle
member.para: Why a separating silence's length carries no information. Real audio has a 3.28 s inter-jingle gap in one chapter and a 1.70 s one in another whose pre-announcement hush is a longer 2.45 s - so the hush before a single jingle and the gap between two consecutive ones cannot be told apart by duration, which is why the walk deliberately does not try.

member.name: IsGenuineSpeech
member.para: What deriving the decoded span from segment timestamps cost. Measured on real audio 2026-07-31: a 0.83 s sting 2 s into one book's jingle and a 0.61 s one 6 s into another's each stopped the retreat where they sounded, leaving both marks inside the music instead of at its leading edge. Both were trusted on VAD duration alone, because a probe opening on the jingle yields exactly one segment which advances to the announcement, so every transient in the music looked "outside the transcript".

member.name: RetreatPastNonSpeech
member.para: What walking through an inter-jingle gap cost. Confirmed against a German test audiobook (2026-07-26) where the retreat previously walked past inter-jingle gaps and landed marks 9-37 s early, in front of the previous chapter's sting, while that book's correctly-marked chapters all have silence-free jingles and are untouched by stopping unconditionally.

What an ends-before silence test cost. Measured on real audio 2026-07-31: a 0.26 s sting starting 0.01 s before its silence ended cost two chapters (in different books, same shape) 2.7 s and 0.9 s, both marks landing at the start of the pre-jingle hush instead of at the jingle itself. That is why a silence qualifies by starting before the position rather than by ending before it.

member.name: ResolveDefaultPhraseOnset
member.para: The split announcement that broke the last-blip rule. On real audio, chapter 31's "Kapitel 31" was split into a 0.67 s "Kapitel" blip and a 0.9 s "31" blip 0.26 s apart, and taking only the last landed the mark after "Kapitel" was already spoken - verified by a 5.25 s re-transcription from that mark, which started mid-narration rather than on the phrase.

The two marks that forced the leading-silence exclusion. Measured 2026-08-02, chapters 6 and 14 of one German audiobook: both regions began where the previous chapter's narration stopped, both had a single swallowed blip 0.7-0.9 s later carrying its last two words, and in both the region's leading silence ended within 3 ms of that blip's own start. Taken as the announcement, each put its mark some twelve to eighteen seconds early, on the previous chapter's closing sentence.
